title: Constraint-Based Scheduling: The Architecture That Makes Production Plans Real
description:
Production plans that look fine in ERP fall apart when a machine fails, a fixture is busy or material is still in inspection. This episode walks manufacturing planners, IT/OT architects and operations leaders through constraint-based scheduling in a hypothetical machining plant, showing how to turn factory facts into rules a scheduling engine can test and produce schedules people can actually run.
In this episode
00:00 – Intro: the ERP date isn't a factory promise06:20 – Plan versus schedule11:34 – Hard and soft constraints22:16 – Routings, BOMs and resource modeling34:10 – Machine state, tooling, labor and material release68:55 – What the scheduling engine solves79:42 – When the five-axis machine fails and constraints collide102:30 – ERP, MES, the scheduling layer and Microsoft architecture
Key takeaways
An ERP date states intent; a finite, constraint-based schedule tests every operation against real resources, tooling, skills, material release and time windows.Hard constraints decide feasibility first, while soft constraints and visible priority policies decide which feasible schedule the plant prefers.ERP, MES and the scheduling layer each keep their own job, with Microsoft Fabric and Power BI providing governed history and visibility rather than acting as the scheduling engine.
